author: TEDx Talks
description:
Evolutionary biologist Justin Garcia argues that we've misdiagnosed the modern "loneliness crisis." It's not a lack of connection — it's a lack of depth. Drawing on research from the Kinsey Institute, he explains why our threat-wired nervous systems are simulating closeness instead of risking real intimacy, and explores what it takes to go deep again.

Dr. Justin Garcia is an evolutionary biologist and international authority on the science of sex and relationships. Since 2019, he has served as the Executive Director of the world-renowned Kinsey Institute, where he is also a Senior Scientist. He holds an appointment as the Ruth N. Halls Professor in the College of Arts and Sciences at Indiana University and is a Founding Co-Director of Human Sexuality and Health at the IU School of Medicine. Dr. Garcia holds a Ph.D. in evolutionary biology and M.S. in biomedical anthropology from Binghamton University and an Executive Certificate in Public Leadership from Harvard Kennedy School. An aw
title: It's not a loneliness epidemic—it's an intimacy crisis | Justin Garcia | TEDxKC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Amidst the chaos around us, my question is: What inner source do we need to make the world a better place? Growing from within, how can we realise a visible, positive impact?
 

My response: by staying true to the fire within us. When we keep working on realising our deepest commitments, we may be able to steer the course of events towards a world we want to leave for future generations.

 

Here, I share with you what I have learned—insights that can help you unleash your potential as you navigate your way through a chaotic world.

 Roland Mees is a Professor of Practice of Business Ethics at the Faculty of Economics and Business at the University of Groningen. Before entering academia, he was Director of Sustainable Finance at ING Wholesale Banking until mid-2025, where he worked closely with CFOs, treasurers, and sustainability managers of major global companies. He is the inventor of the Sustainability-Linked Loan (SLL), a financial product that links loan interest rates to a comp
title: Unleashing Our Potential in a Chaotic World | Roland Mees | TEDxUniversityofGroningen

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Artificial intelligence doesn't just process data — it amplifies whatever mental state you bring to it, turning your noise into professional-looking nonsense.

When you work with your brain's natural rhythms, you unlock the creativity, critical thinking and intuition that AI can amplify but not guide.

The real difference in the age of AI isn't more software — it's a well-regulated human mind doing the leading. Leo van Woerden is a neuroscientist, sleep expert, and speaker with more than 25 years of research experience on the brain, stress, performance, and recovery. His work focuses on a defining challenge of our time: as technology becomes more powerful, how do people remain clear, adaptive, and resilient under increasing pressure?
In his TEDx talk, Leo explores why the real bottleneck is often not the technology itself, but the human system trying to keep up with it. This directly connects to the theme of growth. Real growth does not begin with more speed, more output, or more tool
title: Before You Use AI, Regulate Your Brain | Leo van Woerden | TEDxUniversityofGroningen

author: TEDx Talks
description: Tony Myers is a sustainability professional dedicated to advocating for the power of green careers and working to inspire the next generation to enter the sustainability workforce. Green building initiatives have grown consistently since he joined the field in 2013. Better tech and tighter Building Energy Performance Standards exist, yet the talent pipeline remains thin. Technology gives us the tools, but skilled people give us our future. Tony Myers is a sustainability professional bridging the "Green Skills" gap. Since 2020, he has managed the State of Maryland’s Department of General Services Energy Audit Program, leading eco-initiatives across public facilities. Tony began his energy efficiency career in 2013, progressing from refrigeration upgrades to large commercial retrofits. In 2022, he joined MoCo Green Futures to fight the environmental talent shortage. Through this role, he champions green careers and inspires the next generation to enter the workforce. author: TEDx Talks
description: In this powerful talk, Dr. Sunita Punjabi reveals how the stories we tell ourselves shape our identity, beliefs, and future. Blending neuroscience with personal insight, she shows how we can rewrite those stories and turn adversity into transformation. Dr. Sunita Punjabi, PhD is a neuropsychologist, licensed professional counselor, researcher, and founder of Brain Coach LLC. Her work focuses on neuroplasticity, human behavior, purpose-driven living, and brain optimization. As founder of the Texas Brain Science Symposium, she translates complex neuroscience into practical strategies that help individuals and organizations improve engagement, resilience, and performance. Through research, clinical practice, and speaking engagements, Dr. Punjabi empowers audiences to unlock human potential and create lasting transformation. description: Matthew Kern reflects on his career journey as a chef, from starting as a dishwasher to discovering a passion for fine dining, sustainability, and farm-to-table cooking. Inspired by local farmers and the importance of reducing food waste, he shares how using ingredients thoughtfully can reconnect us to our communities and the stories behind what we eat. Through his philosophy to “leave room for life to happen,” Matthew encourages us to embrace simplicity, find purpose in what we do, and discover peace in learning to live with less. Raised in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, Matt grew up surrounded by food- from homemade pasta, to big family dinners, his passion for food started at an early age and eventually led to his first restaurant job at age 14. Having spent the last 16 years in Coastal Delaware, he has been One Coastal’s Executive Chef and Owner for the past 5 years, leading our kitchen with passion, and a true love of what he is doing. title: Farm to Table | Matthew Kern | TEDxButterfish Cove

description: Why do the people who seem to have everything so often feel the most unseen? Drawing on neuroscience, psychology, and more than a decade of coaching senior leaders, Dr Krishna Athal reveals the five traits that quietly turn extraordinary success into extraordinary isolation, and names “the applause gap”: the distance between how celebrated you are and how known you feel. He closes with three small steps, Audit, Anchor, Allow, for finding your way back to being truly known. Dr Krishna Athal is a scholar-practitioner who works at the intersection of leadership, psychology, neuroscience, and human behavior. He is a life and executive coach, corporate trainer, and leadership consultant who has spent years studying how influence actually operates in real systems, not just in theory, but in boardrooms, teams, institutions, and everyday relationships. His work focuses on sustainable behavioral change, emotional resilience, and practical leadership maturity, helping individuals and organizati
title: The loneliness of success | Dr. Krishna Athal | TEDxButterfish Cove

description: Join Nick McNulty as he discusses the expansion of the EV Charging industry in the United States through his personal lens over the last 15 years. Learn more about the math behind charging times, how much EV infrastructure has grown in the US recently, and some of the exciting EV news on the horizon. Nick McNulty is the Managing Director of Blue Whale EV, where he leads the development and deployment of electric vehicle charging infrastructure projects. With a background in client success, business development, and project management, he has helped municipalities, schools, commercial property owners, and multifamily communities implement EV charging solutions. Nick is passionate about building strategic partnerships that expand access to EV charging. His interest in electrification began at Clarkson University, where he researched EV charging feasibility. author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this TEDx presentation, Max de Stéfani reflects on the dangers of social conformity and the importance of embracing individuality. The speaker shares his experience of celebrating his birthday by exploring Itatiaia National Park with friends, swapping a traditional party for mountain trails and outdoor games,to question why we so often choose to go with the flow and do only what is expected. He references Solomon Asch's famous conformity experiment to demonstrate how group pressure leads people to ignore their own perceptions just to fit in.
Max warns that constantly trying to align with social trends and others' expectations can distance us from who we truly are and stifle creativity. He invites the audience to view authenticity not as something to hide, but to celebrate, reminding us that the most meaningful experiences and world-changing ideas come from challenging expectations rather than following them.
 Grade 7 student at Escola Concept Ribeirão Preto This talk was given at a
title: Who said birthdays need cake? | Max Stéfani | TEDxEscola Concept Ribeirão Preto

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this deeply personal and powerfully reflective talk, Hon. Fatima Lamisula invites the audience to rethink what a “horizon” truly is. Drawing from her own journey, she reveals how the most challenging horizons are not the distant mountains or faraway dreams we imagine, but the invisible beliefs that quietly limit who we think we’re allowed to become.

With honesty and grace, she shares how she once confused sacrifice with disappearance—celebrating everyone else’s growth while neglecting her own. A turning point came when she realized she was grieving the woman she still had the potential to become. That awakening led her to confront the internal stories that had shaped her life and to step boldly into public service.

Through vivid storytelling, she highlights how countless people—women, young leaders, entire communities—live beneath these unseen boundaries. She argues that before systems fail, stories fail, and that leadership begins the moment someone refuses to believe a limiting
title: The Woman Beyond the Horizon | Fatima Bukar Lamisula | TEDxMaiduguri

Her talk offers a grounded reflection on leadership: something shaped long before we step into a role. author: TEDx Talks
description: Africa is home to extraordinary talent, creativity, innovation, and resilience. Yet, despite its enormous potential, the continent continues to confront stereotypes, limiting narratives, and questions about its place in the global economy. In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, Izuchukwu Ukandu, widely known as Coach Izu, challenges Africans to rethink the relationship between identity, excellence, leadership, and global perception. Through What If Excellence Became Africa's Identity?, he explores a powerful idea: Africa's transformation cannot depend solely on changing what the world says about the continent. It must also begin with changing the standards Africans set for themselves, the stories they tell, the institutions they build, and the values they demonstrate through everyday actions. What would happen if excellence became more than an individual achievement? What if it became a shared African mindset, reflected in education, entrepreneurship, innovation, governance, professiona
title: What If Excellence Became Africa's Identity? | Izuchukwu Ukandu | TEDxKubwa

author: TEDx Talks
description: ¿Por qué nos cuesta tanto ser felices si ya tenemos la vida "resuelta"? En esta conmovedora y reflexiva charla, Virginia Cabral nos invita a reevaluar cómo medimos nuestro éxito. A través de anécdotas personales, Virginia contrasta la frágil "escalera de los logros" —alimentada por el ego y los resultados— con el sólido "muro de la plenitud", donde verdaderamente residen la comunidad, la conexión y nuestros valores. Con una profunda sabiduría, nos enseña que vivir es un asunto urgente y que, al final, lo único que nos llevaremos será aquello que hayamos entregado a los demás. Virginia Cabral es una madre, abuela, empresaria y emprendedora dominicana. Más allá de los títulos, Virginia se define a sí misma como una eterna "aprendiz" de la vida. Con casi siete décadas de experiencia, comparte sus vivencias personales y familiares para inspirar a otros a soltar la rigidez, cultivar la esperanza y abrazar la plenitud de lo que ella llama "el arte de la sencillez". This talk was given at a
title: Lo único que te llevarás es lo que hayas entregado | Virginia Cabral | TEDxSantoDomingo

author: TEDx Talks
description: Vivimos en un mundo hiperconectado y obsesionado con la velocidad, donde podemos pedir comida desde un teléfono y recibirla en minutos sin tener que mirar a los ojos a quien la cultivó o cocinó. En esta reveladora charla, el chef Olivier Bur nos invita a frenar y redescubrir que la comida no es solo una forma de nutrirnos, sino una excusa y un lenguaje para conectar verdaderamente con los demás. Compartiendo su experiencia al intentar documentar técnicas tradicionales con productores en San Cristóbal —y su frustración inicial al ver que un proceso artesanal de tres días no se podía acelerar— explica por qué la confianza humana exige tiempo, presencia y paciencia. Su mensaje nos recuerda que, si queremos construir algo verdaderamente irreemplazable, debemos tener la valentía de bajar la velocidad. Olivier Bur es un chef, investigador y emprendedor gastronómico de raíces domínico-suizas, fundador del restaurante de experiencias Casarré en Santo Domingo. Criado entre los contrastes cultu
title: El ingrediente secreto que la eficiencia nos está robando | Olivier Bur | TEDxSantoDomingo

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Safiya Alkali challenges the conventional thinking around preparing children for the future, drawing on her experiences and the realities of growing up in Borno State, Nigeria. She argues that while we constantly speak about preparing children for tomorrow, we rarely question whether we are building a future that is ready for them.

From reimagining teaching methods that inspire curiosity and creativity to creating safe learning environments, strengthening mentorship, and shaping policies that place the next generation at their centre, Safiya makes the case for a fundamental shift in how society invests in children.

She questions the familiar notion that children are simply the leaders of tomorrow, arguing that their future is already being shaped by the decisions we make today. Her message is simple but powerful: Rather than focusing solely on preparing children for the future, we must also take responsibility for preparing the future for them. Safiya Alkali Ajikolo is a child right
title: Is the Future Ready for Children? | Safiya Alkali  Ajikolo | TEDxMaiduguri

author: TEDx Talks
description: ¿Por qué sufrimos cuando intentamos hacer todo de forma perfecta? En esta charla llena de anécdotas y vulnerabilidad, la comediante Patricia Peña explora cómo nuestra ambición puede convertirnos en personas rígidas y resistentes al cambio. A través de una divertida historia personal que la llevó desde una formal conferencia de liderazgo en Nueva York hasta su primer y desastroso intento en un open mic de stand-up, Peña revela cómo aprendió a reírse de sus propios fracasos para vencer la vergüenza. Su mensaje nos recuerda que "la seriedad nos hace fuertes, pero el humor nos hace libres", invitándonos a soltar el control sin abandonar nuestras metas y dándonos el permiso definitivo de ser humanos. Patricia Peña es una profesional que transformó su vida y carrera al descubrir el poder liberador de la comedia. Tras dirigir programas de liderazgo para mujeres y participar en conferencias internacionales, Patricia comprendió que su excesiva seriedad, impulsada por su ambición, se había conv
title: La seriedad te hace fuerte, el humor te hace libre | Patricia Peña | TEDxSantoDomingo

author: TEDx Talks
description: En esta reveladora charla, el ingeniero agrónomo Arturo Bisonó nos demuestra que la verdadera innovación agrícola no solo se trata de tecnología, sino de poner al agricultor en el centro de las soluciones. A través de casos de éxito inspiradores en la República Dominicana, como el de la comunidad agrícola de Villa Poppy, Bisonó explica cómo el acceso a datos climáticos y la investigación participativa permitieron a pequeños productores romper el ciclo de pobreza, logrando cultivar y exportar productos premium como el radicchio a mercados internacionales. Además, nos presenta iniciativas para conectar emocionalmente al consumidor en los restaurantes con las personas que cosechan sus alimentos. Bisonó nos deja una poderosa reflexión: "innovar no solo es hacer algo nuevo, es hacer visible lo que siempre estuvo ahí", recordándonos que, aunque el mundo intente automatizarlo todo, el agricultor sigue siendo irremplazable. Arturo Bisonó es Ingeniero Agrónomo con una maestría (M.Sc.), dedicad
title: Innovar con el agricultor en el centro | Arturo Bisonó | TEDxSantoDomingo

Dr. Pavan Soni is an innovation evangelist, educator, author and founder of Inflexion Point, a firm specialising in design, innovation and leadership. With a doctorate in innovation management from IIM Bangalore, he has worked with organisations across multiple countries and teaches at institutions including ISB Hyderabad and IIM Bangalore. He is the bestselling author of Design Your Thinking, Design Your Career and Everyday Creativity, exploring how creativity and innovation can shape professional and personal growth. This talk invites us to question the narratives we have inherited, recognise the influence of social conditioning, and reconsider the beliefs that limit who we think we can become. It is an exploration of self-discovery and the freedom to define ourselves on our own terms. Mona Verma is an award-winning author, editor, poet and corporate trainer whose work spans literature, leadership and communication. An alumna of Lady Shri Ram College, University of Delhi, she also holds a postgraduate certification from Harvard Business School. She has authored several books and contributed to numerous anthologies, while serving as an executive presence coach and leadership skills facilitator through DISHA. This talk explores the difference between constant communication and feeling truly seen, heard, and understood. It examines why meaningful relationships require more than digital access, highlighting the importance of empathy, vulnerability, presence, and the willingness to connect beyond the surface. Dr. Shalini J. Sharma is a counselling psychologist and trauma-trained psychotherapist with over two decades of professional experience. She serves as Director of Wellness at Plaksha University, where she works to support psychological well-being and foster a supportive environment for students, faculty and staff. With expertise in emotional intelligence, resilience and human behaviour, she brings together psychological insights and practical approaches to emotional well-being and personal development. She is also a published author of children's books that encourage young readers

description: In this compelling TEDx talk, Irene Evadine Ngong Bonjeh introduces The Human Currency, a powerful perspective on the value of authentic storytelling, trust, empathy, and the relationships that shape our lives. Drawing from her experience in communications, sustainability, and international development, Irene challenges the belief that visibility equals impact. She explores why being seen is not the same as being understood, why information alone rarely inspires transformation, and why the stories we tell matter most when they create genuine human connection. At the heart of her message is a thought-provoking idea: Our greatest influence may not come from how many people hear us, but from how deeply we connect with those who do. The Human Currency invites us to rethink what makes communication valuable, how trust is built, and why meaningful relationships remain essential in an increasingly digital and disconnected world. Irene Evadine Ngong Bonjeh is a communications and sustainabili

Her journey raises questions many of us quietly wrestle with: How much of who we are is shaped by the expectations of others? What happens when our calling demands that we step beyond familiar spaces? And how do we find the courage to embrace our authentic identity? Unmasked is more than a story of entrepreneurship or personal achievement. This talk examines how a new generation is reshaping ideas about identity, success, work, relationships, and social responsibility. It explores the possibilities and challenges of a generation seeking not simply to adapt to the world it inherits, but to actively redefine it. Kulbhushan Kain is an award-winning educationist, author and columnist with over four decades of experience in school education in India and abroad. He is the author of *A Lifetime in Schools: Few Canes, Lots of Sugarcane*, a reflective account of his experiences in education and leadership. description: In this powerful and deeply personal TEDx talk, Dr. Ifeoma Elizabeth Dan-Ogosi takes us on a journey from exclusion to empowerment, revealing what becomes possible when rejection is transformed into purpose. The Girl They Silenced, Built the Room Anyway is more than a story of academic achievement. It is a compelling exploration of belonging, identity, courage, and the responsibility to create spaces where others do not have to fight to be heard. Drawing from over sixteen years of experience in higher education, Dr. Ifeoma challenges us to reconsider what true inclusion means. What if the problem is not that some people do not belong, but that the rooms we have built were never designed to welcome them? And what if, instead of waiting for permission to enter, we dared to build something different? author: TEDx Talks
description: Former high school science teacher Jason Jurey spent 17 years teaching students about food systems without planting a single crop, until seven classroom hydroponic systems changed how his students saw science. In this talk, he shares what happens when kids are handed something living to take care of instead of a worksheet, and why the generation that will have to feed billions needs that experience now. Jason Jurey has nearly two decades of experience in environmental education and is a controlled environment agriculture specialist.  He travels the county helping school districts set up indoor gardening programs to address food security and elevate STEM learning experiences.  Jason holds a Bachelor of Science in wildlife biology, master’s degree in secondary education and a master’s degree in environmental science.  He enjoys spending his free time growing microgreens and gourmet mushrooms for friends and family. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but
title: Grow What Matters | Jason Jurey | TEDxButterfish Cove

author: TEDx Talks
description: We scroll past thousands of images a day, and the female figure travels through them fastest, a pattern art history set long before algorithms did. For centuries, women were the subjects of paintings but rarely the painters. Painter Allison Zuckerman cuts apart works by male Old Masters, from Rubens to Michelangelo, and rebuilds their women as protagonists who look back. When her own paintings were resold at auction without her say, one falling from $212,000 to $20,000 in two and a half years, she remixed those too, layering them into a new sculpture. She argues that the stories handed to us are only source material, and that remixing them is resilience and power. Allison Zuckerman is a contemporary artist with a plethora of pop-surrealist pieces. Her work connects painting and digital mediums to challenge gender stereotypes and dominant narratives. A Penn alum currently based in New York City, her work has been displayed in galleries internationally and has expanded to the music and
title: Remixing and reclaiming the female figure | Allison Zuckerman | TEDxPenn
